title: HTML Paragraphs
summary: A paragraph groups sentences about one idea. HTML uses the p tag to mark a paragraph.
introduction: A paragraph groups sentences about one idea. HTML uses the p tag to mark a paragraph. Write two short paragraphs. Learn why pressing Enter in the code does not always make a new line on the page.
learningObjectives: Write paragraphs and understand whitespace collapsing
Insert line breaks with br only where a break is part of the content
Use pre for preformatted text and blockquote for quotations

blocks.text:
A `

` element holds one paragraph of text. Browsers display it as a block with space above and below, so you never need empty paragraphs or line breaks to separate paragraphs.

blocks.code:
HTML paragraphs are blocks of text.

Each one starts on a new line with space around it.

blocks.text: Inside most elements, any run of spaces, tabs and line breaks in your source is shown as a single space. This lets you format your source code freely without affecting the page.

Pressing Enter in your editor does not create a line break on the page, and typing five spaces does not indent text. If you need visual spacing, use CSS; if the break is genuinely part of the content, use `
`.

blocks.title: Not for spacing
blocks.text:
`


` to push content down is a classic beginner habit. Screen readers announce each break, and the spacing breaks on different screen sizes. Use CSS margins instead.
The `<pre>` element preserves spaces and line breaks exactly as written and uses a monospaced font. It is the right choice for code listings, ASCII diagrams and anything where alignment matters.

For code, combine `
` with ``: `
…
`. The `
` keeps the layout and the `` says what the content is.
`<blockquote>` marks a quotation that stands on its own as a block; the optional `cite` attribute holds the source URL. `<q>` is for short inline quotes, and browsers add the quotation marks for you.

blocks.title: When text is not a paragraph
blocks.text:
A heading, a list item, a table cell and a button each have their own element. Reserve `

` for actual prose; wrapping everything in paragraphs makes the structure meaningless.
